```{r}
source("R/utils.R")
```

```{r}
state_name <- "United States"
state_name_text <- "the United States"

srs_state_new <- read_rds(csg_sp_path("jr_data_library", "data", "analysis", "fbi", "srs", "fbi_srs_estimated_crimes_state.rds")) |> 
  mutate(crime_cat = if_else(group %in% c("Aggravated assault", "Homicide", "Rape", "Robbery"), "Violent", "Property")) |> 
  select(-state_fips, -group_cat, -starts_with("rate")) |> 
  filter(indicator != "Unsolved rate") |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = indicator, values_from = n) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  select(
    year, state_name, state_abbr, group, crime_cat, pop_total, pop_adult,
    incidents_reported, incidents_unsolved, incidents_cleared) |> 
  mutate(
    pct_unsolved = incidents_unsolved / incidents_reported,
    incidents_reported_rate_total = incidents_reported / pop_total,
    incidents_reported_rate_adult = incidents_reported / pop_adult
  )

### time series use an 11-year window ending in the latest data year
srs_by_cat_us <- srs_state_new |>
  filter(crime_cat == "Violent", year >= max(year) - 10) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarize(
    pop_total = sum(pop_total[group == "Homicide"], na.rm = TRUE),
    across(c(incidents_reported, incidents_unsolved), \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  ) |>
  mutate(
    incidents_reported_rate_total = incidents_reported / pop_total,
    incidents_solved = incidents_reported - incidents_unsolved,
    pct_solved = incidents_solved / incidents_reported
  )

srs_us <- srs_state_new |>
  filter(crime_cat == "Violent", year >= max(year) - 10) |>
  group_by(year, group) |>
  summarize(
    across(c(pop_total, incidents_reported, incidents_unsolved), \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    incidents_reported_rate_total = incidents_reported / pop_total,
    incidents_solved = incidents_reported - incidents_unsolved,
    pct_solved = incidents_solved / incidents_reported
  )

### state maps and table compare the pre-pandemic base year to the latest year
base_year <- 2019
latest_year <- max(srs_state_new$year)

### states without reliable clearance data in the base or latest year
states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz <- c("Illinois")

### aggregate counts and create rates by state for the base and latest years
### keeping values from each year for tooltips
srs_state_to_map <- srs_state_new |>
  filter(crime_cat == "Violent", year %in% c(base_year, latest_year)) |>
  group_by(state_name, state_abbr, pop_total, year) |>
  summarize(
    n_reported = sum(incidents_reported, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_cleared = sum(incidents_cleared, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_unsolved = sum(incidents_unsolved, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  ### calculate rates
  mutate(
    solved_rate = n_cleared / n_reported,
    viol_crime_rate_100k = (n_reported / pop_total) * 100000
  ) |>
  group_by(state_name) |>
  ### solve rates are multiplied by 100 for highcharts formatting
  mutate(
    n_reported_base = n_reported[year == base_year],
    n_reported_latest = n_reported[year == latest_year],
    n_solved_base = n_cleared[year == base_year],
    n_solved_latest = n_cleared[year == latest_year],
    viol_crime_rate_100k_base = viol_crime_rate_100k[year == base_year],
    viol_crime_rate_100k_latest = viol_crime_rate_100k[year == latest_year],
    solved_rate_base = solved_rate[year == base_year] * 100,
    solved_rate_latest = solved_rate[year == latest_year] * 100,
    solved_rate_percent_point_change = solved_rate_latest - solved_rate_base,
    viol_crime_rate_percent_change = (viol_crime_rate_100k_latest - viol_crime_rate_100k_base) / viol_crime_rate_100k_base * 100
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ### keep one row per state with latest-year population
  filter(year == latest_year)

### percent change from the first to the last year of a series
pct_change_first_last <- function(x, year) {
  (x[year == max(year)] - x[year == min(year)]) / x[year == min(year)]
}

### describe a set of states for text, e.g., "12 states and the District of Columbia"
describe_states <- function(abbr) {
  n <- sum(abbr != "DC")
  paste0(n, if_else(n == 1, " state", " states"), if_else("DC" %in% abbr, " and the District of Columbia", ""))
}

states_rate_down <- srs_state_to_map |> filter(viol_crime_rate_percent_change < 0) |> pull(state_abbr)
states_rate_up <- srs_state_to_map |> filter(viol_crime_rate_percent_change > 0) |> pull(state_abbr)

states_solved <- srs_state_to_map |> filter(!state_name %in% states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz)
states_solved_down <- states_solved |> filter(solved_rate_percent_point_change < 0) |> pull(state_abbr)
states_solved_up <- states_solved |> filter(solved_rate_percent_point_change > 0) |> pull(state_abbr)


min_max_viol_crime <- srs_by_cat_us |>
  filter(year %in% c(min(year), max(year))) |>
  arrange(year)

max_year <- min_max_viol_crime$year[2]
min_year <- min_max_viol_crime$year[1]

pct_change <-
  (min_max_viol_crime$incidents_reported[2] - min_max_viol_crime$incidents_reported[1]) / min_max_viol_crime$incidents_reported[1]

change_text <- case_when(
  pct_change > 0.005  ~ paste0(percent(abs(pct_change), 1),
                               " more"),
  pct_change < -0.005 ~ paste0(percent(abs(pct_change), 1),
                               " fewer"),
  TRUE                ~ "nearly the same number of"
)

pct_change_solved <-
  min_max_viol_crime$pct_solved[2] - min_max_viol_crime$pct_solved[1]

change_text_solved <- case_when(
  pct_change_solved > 0.005 &
    pct_change_solved < 0.015 ~ paste0(comma(abs(
      pct_change_solved * 100
    ), 1),
    " percentage point higher than"),
  pct_change_solved >= 0.015  ~ paste0(comma(abs(
    pct_change_solved * 100
  ), 1),
  " percentage points higher than"),
  pct_change_solved < -0.005 &
    pct_change_solved > -0.015 ~ paste0(comma(abs(
      pct_change_solved * 100
    ), 1),
    " percentage point lower than"),
  pct_change_solved <= -0.015 ~ paste0(comma(abs(
    pct_change_solved * 100
  ), 1),
  " percentage points lower than"),
  TRUE                      ~ "nearly the same as"
)

### national violent crime rate change and offenses lower or higher than the base year
us_rate_change <- srs_by_cat_us |>
  filter(year %in% c(base_year, latest_year)) |>
  summarize(change = pct_change_first_last(incidents_reported_rate_total, year)) |>
  pull(change)

offense_rate_change <- srs_us |>
  filter(year %in% c(base_year, latest_year)) |>
  summarize(change = incidents_reported_rate_total[year == latest_year] - incidents_reported_rate_total[year == base_year], .by = group)

offenses_lower <- offense_rate_change |> filter(change < 0) |> pull(group) |> tolower()
offenses_higher <- offense_rate_change |> filter(change > 0) |> pull(group) |> tolower()

max_viol_crime_off <- srs_us |>
  filter(year == max(year)) |>
  arrange(desc(incidents_reported)) |>
  mutate(pct = incidents_reported / sum(incidents_reported))

### import and prep hex map geo
hex <- sf::read_sf("us_states_hexgrid.geojson") |>
  select(state_abb = iso3166_2)

hex_gj <- hex |>
  sf::st_transform(3857) |>
  geojsonsf::sf_geojson() |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON(simplifyVector = FALSE)

axis_expansion_mult <- 0.5
```

```{r }
### import C-CPI-U index for inflation-adjusting expenditures
### from: https://www.census.gov/topics/income-poverty/income/guidance/current-vs-constant-dollars.html
### first 4 characters of year drop footnote markers (e.g., "20252" is 2025)
inflation_index_years <- readxl::read_xls(
  csg_sp_path("JR_Clearance_Rates", "Data", "annual-index-value_annual-percent-change_2025.xls"),
  skip = 2
) |>
  select(year = 1, inflation_index = 2) |>
  mutate(year = as.numeric(str_sub(year, 1, 4))) |>
  filter(!is.na(year), !is.na(inflation_index))

### import asslgf_clean_national for lea expenditure analysis
### national police protection expenditures in dollars of the latest survey year
asslgf_clean_national <- read_rds(csg_sp_path("jr_data_library", "data", "analysis", "census", "asslgf", "census_asslgf_state.rds")) |>
  filter(
    indicator == "Expenditures",
    group == "Police Protection",
    geo_abbr == "US",
    year >= max(year) - 10
  ) |>
  left_join(inflation_index_years, by = "year") |>
  mutate(
    n_inflation_adjusted_latest_year_dollars = n * inflation_index[year == max(year)] / inflation_index,
    inflation_adjusted_rate_total = n_inflation_adjusted_latest_year_dollars / pop_total
  )

### national violent crime counts for officer workload
violent_us_by_year <- srs_state_new |>
  filter(crime_cat == "Violent") |>
  summarize(n_violent_reported = sum(incidents_reported, na.rm = TRUE), .by = year)

### import ucr_employee_data_national_clean for officer workload analysis
### officer rates use the population covered by reporting agencies
### officers per violent crime divides the covered officer rate by the national violent crime rate
ucr_employee_data_national_clean <- read_rds(csg_sp_path("jr_data_library", "data", "analysis", "fbi", "lee", "fbi_lee_state.rds")) |>
  filter(geo_abbr == "US", group == "Officers", year >= max(year) - 10) |>
  left_join(violent_us_by_year, by = "year") |>
  mutate(
    officer_pop_rate_per_10k = rate_covered * 10000,
    officer_per_violent_offense_1k = rate_covered / (n_violent_reported / pop_total) * 1000
  ) |>
  arrange(year)
```


```{r }
### import shr homicide incidents and clearances by state, year, and group
### homicide charts pool 2022 on because SHR coverage is low in 2021
shr_state <- read_rds(csg_sp_path("jr_data_library", "data", "analysis", "fbi", "shr", "fbi_shr_state.rds"))

shr_first_year <- 2022
shr_years <- paste0(shr_first_year, "–", max(shr_state$year))

shr_source <- paste0("FBI UCR Program, Supplementary Homicide Reports (", shr_years, ")")
shr_panels <- list(
  race = list(
    category = "victim_race_eth", title = "Homicide solve rates by race and ethnicity",
    caption = paste0("This analysis excludes records where a victim's race and ethnicity is unknown<br>", shr_source)
  ),
  gender = list(
    category = "victim_sex", title = "Homicide solve rates by gender",
    caption = paste0("This analysis excludes records where a victim's gender is unknown<br>", shr_source)
  ),
  age = list(
    category = "victim_age", title = "Homicide solve rates by age",
    caption = paste0("This analysis excludes records where a victim's age is unknown<br>", shr_source),
    order = c("Under 25", "25 to 34", "35 to 45", "46+")
  ),
  weapon = list(
    category = "weapon", title = "Homicide solve rates by weapon",
    caption = paste0("This analysis includes the most common weapons across states in recent years<br>", shr_source),
    exclude = "Other", sort_desc = TRUE
  ),
  victims = list(
    category = "victim_count", title = "Homicide solve rates by number of victims",
    caption = shr_source, order = c("Single victim", "Multiple victims"),
    categories = c("Single victim", "Multiple victims")
  )
)

```


# Trends in Violent Crime and Accountability

## 50-state violent crime data

::: {.panel-tabset}

## `r base_year`–`r latest_year` change

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5.5

# Assign colors
darkorange  <- "#7B3014"
orange      <- "#D25E2D"
lightorange <- "#EDB799"
white       <- "#FFFFFF"
lightblue   <- "#9ed4ef"
regblue     <- "#007392"
darkblue    <- "#00475d"
blue1       <- "#d4e9f8"
blue2       <- "#9ed4ef"
blue4       <- "#007392"
blue5       <- "#00475d"

change_colors <- c(darkblue, regblue, lightblue, white, lightorange, orange, darkorange)
rate_colors <- c(blue1, blue2, blue4, blue5)
state_map_specs <- list(
  crime_change = list(
    value = "viol_crime_rate_percent_change",
    title = paste0("Change in violent crime, ", base_year, "–", latest_year),
    subtitle = "Percent change in crime reported to police per 100,000 residents",
    caption = "FBI UCR Program, state crime estimates",
    colors = change_colors, label_format = "{value}%", legend_width = 250,
    accessibility = "state: {point.state_name}, percent change: {point.value:.1f}",
    symmetric = TRUE
  ),
  crime_rate = list(
    value = "viol_crime_rate_100k_latest",
    title = paste0("Violent crime rate, ", latest_year),
    subtitle = "Crime reported to police per 100,000 residents",
    caption = "FBI UCR Program, state crime estimates",
    colors = rate_colors, label_format = "{value:,.0f}", legend_width = 250,
    accessibility = "state: {point.state_name}, violent crime rate: {point.value:.1f}"
  ),
  solve_change = list(
    value = "solved_rate_percent_point_change",
    title = paste0("Change in percentage of violent crime solved, ", base_year, "–", latest_year),
    subtitle = paste0("Percentage point change in rate of solved violent crimes from ", base_year, " to ", latest_year),
    caption = "FBI UCR Program, state crime estimates and clearances",
    colors = rev(change_colors), label_format = "{value}", legend_width = 300,
    accessibility = "state: {point.state_name}, percent point change: {point.value:.1f}",
    symmetric = TRUE, null_interaction = TRUE
  ),
  solve_rate = list(
    value = "solved_rate_latest",
    title = paste0("Solved violent crime, ", latest_year),
    subtitle = "Percentage of violent crimes solved",
    caption = "FBI UCR Program, state crime estimates and clearances",
    colors = rate_colors, label_format = "{value}%", legend_width = 400,
    accessibility = "state: {point.state_name}, solve rate: {point.value:.1f}",
    null_interaction = TRUE
  )
)

### add tooltip
srs_state_to_map_2 <- srs_state_to_map |>
  ### add '+" in front of positive numbers and 0
  ### only for value we'll include in tooltip
  mutate(
    viol_crime_rate_percent_change_clean = as.numeric(comma(
      viol_crime_rate_percent_change, 1
    )),
    viol_crime_rate_percent_change_clean = sprintf("%+3d%%", viol_crime_rate_percent_change_clean),
    tooltip = paste0(
      "<b>", state_name, "</b><br>",
      "Change in violent crime rate: ",
      viol_crime_rate_percent_change_clean,
      "<br>",
      "Violent incidents per 100k (", latest_year, "): ",
      comma(viol_crime_rate_100k_latest, 1),
      "<br>",
      "Violent incidents per 100k (", base_year, "): ",
      comma(viol_crime_rate_100k_base, 1)
    ),
    url = paste0("https://projects.csgjusticecenter.org/tools-for-states-to-address-crime/50-state-crime-data/?state=", tolower(state_abbr))
  )

state_map_chart(srs_state_to_map_2, hex_gj, state_map_specs$crime_change)
```

## `r latest_year` crime rate

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5.5

### add tooltip
srs_state_to_map_1 <- srs_state_to_map |> 
  ### add '+" in front of positive numbers and 0
  ### only for value we'll include in tooltip
  mutate(
    viol_crime_rate_percent_change_clean = as.numeric(comma(viol_crime_rate_percent_change,1)),
    viol_crime_rate_percent_change_clean = sprintf("%+3d%%", viol_crime_rate_percent_change_clean),
    tooltip = paste0(
      "<b>", state_name, " – ", latest_year, "</b><br>",
      "Violent incidents per 100k: ", comma(viol_crime_rate_100k_latest, 1), "<br>",
      "Violent incidents reported: ", comma(n_reported_latest, 1), "<br>"
      ),
    url = paste0("https://projects.csgjusticecenter.org/tools-for-states-to-address-crime/50-state-crime-data/?state=", tolower(state_abbr))
    )

state_map_chart(srs_state_to_map_1, hex_gj, state_map_specs$crime_rate)
```

:::

The national violent crime rate was `r percent(abs(us_rate_change), 1, suffix = " percent")` `r if_else(us_rate_change < 0, "lower", "higher")` in `r latest_year` than in `r base_year`. In `r latest_year`, rates of `r knitr::combine_words(offenses_lower)` were lower than in `r base_year``r if (length(offenses_higher) > 0) paste0(", while the rate of ", knitr::combine_words(offenses_higher), " was higher")`.

Trends in violent crime also varied by state. Between `r base_year` and `r latest_year`, violent crime rates decreased in `r describe_states(states_rate_down)` and increased in `r describe_states(states_rate_up)`.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## `r base_year`–`r latest_year` change

## `r latest_year` solve rate

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5.5

### add tooltip
srs_state_to_map_3 <- srs_state_to_map |> 
  ### filter out states in states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz
  mutate(solved_rate_latest = if_else(
    state_name %in% states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz,
    NA_real_, solved_rate_latest
  )) |>
  ### add '+" in front of positive numbers and 0
  ### only for value we'll include in tooltip
  mutate(
    tooltip = if_else(!state_name %in% states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz,
                     paste0(
      "<b>", state_name, " – ", latest_year, "</b><br>",
      "Solve rate: ", comma(solved_rate_latest, 1),"%", "<br>",
      "Violent incidents reported: ", comma(n_reported_latest, 1), "<br>",
      "Violent incidents solved: ", comma(n_solved_latest, 1)
      ),
      paste0(
      state_name, " did not report enough data", "<br>",
      "on solved crime to the FBI to", "<br>",
      "make reliable estimates."
      )
    ),
    url = paste0("https://projects.csgjusticecenter.org/tools-for-states-to-address-crime/50-state-crime-data/?state=", tolower(state_abbr)))

state_map_chart(srs_state_to_map_3, hex_gj, state_map_specs$solve_rate)
```

:::

Between `r base_year` and `r latest_year`, the percentage of violent crimes solved by law enforcement increased in `r describe_states(states_solved_up)` and decreased in `r describe_states(states_solved_down)`.

`r knitr::combine_words(states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz)` did not report enough data to the FBI on whether crimes were solved to make reliable estimates.

## Trends in reported violent crime

In `r max(srs_by_cat_us$year)`, `r srs_by_cat_us |> filter(year == max(year)) |> pull(incidents_reported_rate_total) |> comma(scale = 1e5)` violent crime incidents per 100,000 residents were reported to police in the United States.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## All violent crime

```{r}
to_plot <- srs_by_cat_us |> 
  mutate(
    incidents_reported_rate_total = incidents_reported_rate_total * 1e5,
    tooltip = paste0(
      "<b>", state_name, " – ", year, "</b><br>",
      "Violent incidents per 100k: ", comma(incidents_reported_rate_total, 1), "<br>",
      "Violent incidents reported: ", comma(incidents_reported, 1)
      ),
    state_name = fct_relevel(state_name, "United States", after = Inf)
    )

rng <- range(to_plot$incidents_reported_rate_total)
mult <- diff(rng) * axis_expansion_mult

y_min <- rng[1] - mult
y_max <- rng[2] + mult

to_plot |> 
  hchart(
    "spline",
    hcaes(year, incidents_reported_rate_total),
    color = jr_pal[1],
    accessibility = list(
      point = list(
        valueDescriptionFormat = "{point.state}, year: {point.x:.0f}, rate: {point.y:.1f}"
        )
      )
  ) |> 
  hc_title(text = paste0("Violent crime in ", state_name_text)) |>
  hc_subtitle(text = "Crime reported to police per 100,000 residents") |> 
  hc_caption(text = "FBI UCR Program, state crime estimates") |>
  hc_yAxis(
    min = y_min,
    max = y_max,
    endOnTick = FALSE
  ) |>
  hc_setup()
```


```{r}
to_plot <- srs_us |> 
  left_join(offense_pal, by = c("group" = "crime")) |> 
  group_by(year) |> 
  mutate(tot_crime = sum(incidents_reported)) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  mutate(
    pct = incidents_reported / tot_crime,
    incidents_reported_rate_total = incidents_reported_rate_total * 1e5,
    group = fct_reorder(group, incidents_reported_rate_total),
    tooltip = paste0(
      "<b>", group, " – ", year, "</b></br>",
      "Incidents reported per 100k: ", comma(incidents_reported_rate_total, 1), "<br>",
      "Incidents reported: ", comma(incidents_reported, 1), "<br>",
      "Total violent incidents reported: ", comma(tot_crime, 1), "<br>",
      "Share of all violent incidents: ", percent(pct, 1)
      )
    ) |> 
  arrange(year, group)
```

## Aggravated assault

## Trends in solved violent crime

In `r max(srs_by_cat_us$year)`, `r srs_by_cat_us |> filter(year == max(year)) |> pull(pct_solved) |> percent(suffix = " percent")` of violent crime incidents reported to police in the United States were solved. The percentage of violent crimes that law enforcement solved fell from 2019 to 2022 and increased in `r max(srs_by_cat_us$year)` to its highest level since at least `r min(srs_by_cat_us$year)`.

The following tables include violent crime rates and solve rates by state and offense. For more information on violent crime solve rates for each offense by state, [visit state-specific pages here](https://projects.csgjusticecenter.org/tools-for-states-to-address-crime/50-state-crime-data/).

```{r}

### create state-level table
srs_state_to_map |> 
    select(
      state_name,
      viol_crime_rate_100k_latest,
      n_reported_latest,
      viol_crime_rate_percent_change,
      solved_rate_latest,
      solved_rate_percent_point_change
      ) |> 
   ### recode all solved incident data to NA if state %in% states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz
  mutate(
    across(solved_rate_latest:solved_rate_percent_point_change,
                ~ if_else(state_name%in%states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz,
                          NA, .)
           )
    ) |> 
  reactable_template(
    sort_col = list("state_name" = "asc"),
    columns = list(
      state_name = colDef(name = "State"),
      viol_crime_rate_100k_latest = colDef(name = paste0("Violent Incidents per 100k (", latest_year, ")")), 
      n_reported_latest = colDef(name = paste0("Violent Incidents Reported (", latest_year, ")")), 
      viol_crime_rate_percent_change = colDef(
        name = paste0("Percent change in violent crime rate (", base_year, " to ", latest_year, ")"),
        cell = add_plus_sign_percent_change
        ),
      solved_rate_latest = colDef(
        name = paste0("Solve Rate (", latest_year, ")"),
        format = colFormat(suffix = "%", digits = 0)
        ),
      solved_rate_percent_point_change = colDef(
        name = paste0("Percentage point change in solve rate (", base_year, " to ", latest_year, ")"),
        cell = add_plus_sign_percent_point_change,
        )
      )
    )

```

```{r, results='asis'}
cat("### By offense")
```


<span style="color:#E17619"> Orange </span> indicates a solve rate less than the state average across the United States.

<span style="color:#15607A"> Blue </span> indicates a solve rate greater than or equal to the state average across the United States.


```{r}
###################################################################################
### prep srs_state_by_offense_latest for table
###################################################################################

### reported rates per 100k and solve rates by state and violent offense type
### cap solve rates at 1
srs_state_by_offense_latest <- srs_state_new |>
  filter(crime_cat == "Violent", year == latest_year) |>
  mutate(
    solved_rate = pmin((incidents_reported - incidents_unsolved) / incidents_reported, 1),
    n_reported_rate = incidents_reported / pop_total * 100000
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = state_name,
    names_from = group,
    values_from = c(n_reported_rate, solved_rate)
  ) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  ### recode all solved incident data to NA if state %in% states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz
  mutate(
    across(c(solved_rate_aggravated_assault,
             solved_rate_homicide,
             solved_rate_rape,
             solved_rate_robbery),
                ~ if_else(state_name%in%states_to_exclude_from_solved_rate_viz,
                          NA, .)))

### determine median solve rates by violent offense type for state
### we'll use these state averages to develop an agency-level comparison in the table
state_median_solved_rate_aggravated_assault <- median(srs_state_by_offense_latest$solved_rate_aggravated_assault,
                                                      na.rm=TRUE)

state_median_solved_rate_homicide <- median(srs_state_by_offense_latest$solved_rate_homicide,
                                                      na.rm=TRUE)

state_median_solved_rate_rape <- median(srs_state_by_offense_latest$solved_rate_rape,
                                                      na.rm=TRUE)

state_median_solved_rate_robbery <- median(srs_state_by_offense_latest$solved_rate_robbery,
                                                      na.rm=TRUE)


### final prep df for table
srs_state_by_offense_latest |> 
  mutate(across(c(solved_rate_aggravated_assault,
                  solved_rate_homicide,
                  solved_rate_rape,
                  solved_rate_robbery
                  ), 
                ~ replace(.x, is.nan(.x), NA))
         ) |> 
  reactable_template(
    sort_col = list("state_name" = "asc"),
    columns = list(
      state_name = colDef(name = "State", minWidth = 250,
                             sticky = "left",
      # Add a right border style to visually distinguish the sticky column
      style = list(borderRight = "1px solid #eee"),
      headerStyle = list(borderRight = "1px solid #eee")),
      n_reported_rate_aggravated_assault = colDef(name = "Aggravated Assault Incidents per 100k",
                               format = colFormat(digits = 0, separators = TRUE), minWidth = 120), 
      solved_rate_aggravated_assault = solve_rate_column("Aggravated Assault", state_median_solved_rate_aggravated_assault),
      n_reported_rate_homicide = colDef(name = "Homicide Incidents per 100k",
                               format = colFormat(digits = 0, separators = TRUE), 
                               align = "center",
          ),
      solved_rate_homicide = solve_rate_column("Homicide", state_median_solved_rate_homicide, align = "center"),

      n_reported_rate_rape = colDef(name = "Rape Incidents per 100k",
                               format = colFormat(digits = 0, separators = TRUE)),
      solved_rate_rape = solve_rate_column("Rape", state_median_solved_rate_rape, min_width = 155, align = "left"),
      n_reported_rate_robbery = colDef(name = "Robbery Incidents per 100k",
                               format = colFormat(digits = 0, separators = TRUE)), 
      solved_rate_robbery = solve_rate_column("Robbery", state_median_solved_rate_robbery)
    ))
```

:::

Data regarding crime and solve rates come from the FBI's [Uniform Crime Reporting Program](https://www.fbi.gov/how-we-can-help-you/need-an-fbi-service-or-more-information/ucr). Violent crime includes homicide, aggravated assault, robbery, and rape. Crime rates are calculated by dividing the number of estimated incidents by the total population for a given geography. Solve rates are the number of reported crimes cleared by arrest or by exceptional means divided by the number of reported crimes. For more information, see the data sources and methodology section below.

## Data sources and methodology

Data regarding crime and solve rates come from the FBI's [Uniform Crime Reporting Program](https://www.fbi.gov/how-we-can-help-you/need-an-fbi-service-or-more-information/ucr){target="_parent"}. Counts of reported violent crime between `r min(srs_by_cat_us$year)` and `r latest_year` are derived from the Summary Reporting System (SRS) and the National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS). The FBI estimates reported crime for each state from agency-level reports, accounting for agencies that did not report, and publishes these estimates through `r latest_year` on its [Crime Data Explorer](https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/webapp/#/pages/downloads){target="_parent"}. Solve rates apply each state's clearance rate among agencies that reported to the FBI, from the Crime Data Explorer, to the FBI's state estimates of reported crime.

The FBI stopped SRS data collection after data year 2020 and required law enforcement agencies to use NIBRS to report crime statistics to the FBI. This change decreased the number of agencies that submitted their crime data and thus reduced the reliability of state estimates in 2021. From 2022 through 2024, the FBI allowed agencies who were unable to submit NIBRS data to submit SRS data again. Ninety-six percent of the U.S. population was covered in the 2024 crime data submissions to the FBI, with most states providing close to complete data. However, the population upon which the estimates were derived decreased by over 10 percent in three states: Florida, Mississippi, and Wyoming, so conclusions about crime changes in those states should be interpreted with additional caution.

Crime rates are calculated by dividing the number of estimated incidents by the total population. Population data come from the U.S. Census Bureau [Population Estimates Program](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest.html){target="_parent"}.

Solve rates are the number of reported crimes cleared by arrest or by exceptional means divided by the number of reported crimes. A reported crime incident is [cleared by exceptional means](https://ucr.fbi.gov/crime-in-the-u.s/2019/crime-in-the-u.s.-2019/topic-pages/clearances){target='_parent'} if a law enforcement agency is unable to arrest or formally charge a person with a crime, but the agency has met the following conditions:
    
a) Identified the person who committed the crime
b) Gathered enough evidence to support an arrest, make a charge, and turn over the person to the court for prosecution
c) Identified the suspect’s exact location so that the person could be taken into custody immediately
d) Encountered a circumstance outside the control of law enforcement that prohibits the agency from arresting, charging, and prosecuting the person
    
Examples of exceptional clearances include the death of the person who committed the crime; the victim’s refusal to cooperate with the prosecution after the person who committed the crime has been identified; or the denial of extradition.

Data regarding law enforcement expenditures were downloaded from the U.S. Census Bureau [Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/gov-finances.html){target="_parent"}. Expenditures include police protection spending by state governments and all local governments in each state, such as counties and municipalities. Expenditures are adjusted for inflation to constant dollars of the most recent year using the Chained Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (C-CPI-U), following the [Census Bureau's guidance](https://www.census.gov/topics/income-poverty/income/guidance/current-vs-constant-dollars.html){target="_parent"}.

Officer employment analysis is restricted to sworn officers in state and local law enforcement agencies, as of October 31 of each year, and was downloaded from the FBI's [Crime Data Explorer law enforcement employee data](https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/webapp/#/pages/downloads){target="_parent"}. Officers per capita use the population served by agencies that reported employee counts. Officers per violent crime divide that rate by the national violent crime rate from the SRS state estimates.

Data on homicide solve rates and case characteristics come from the FBI's [Supplementary Homicide Reports (SHR)](https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/webapp/#/pages/downloads){target="_parent"}. The analysis includes murder and nonnegligent manslaughter incidents and excludes manslaughter by negligence. SHR data do not record clearances, so a homicide is counted as solved when the offender's age, sex, and race are known. Solve rates combine data from 2022 through the most recent year. Data from 2021 are excluded because many large states did not report SHR data during the transition to NIBRS.

:::
